title: Managers' Choices of Performance Measures in Promotion Decisions: An Analysis of Alternative Job Assignments

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow. The supplied variant contains an online theoretical appendix only; no runnable workflow, entry point, or input construction is included.

requirements.description: The empirical specification refers to employee-year PERFORMANCE, ABILITY, and PROMTYPE measures, but the package does not identify the analysis file/source, required fields as stored, observation coverage, or their construction. The appendix alone cannot establish a compatible input route.

issues.description: The supplied package inventory contains only the online appendix PDF. It provides no executable source, README/data guide, entry point, stage order, or specification of the analysis input route, so dependency closure and executable workflow are unresolved.

evidence.description: The appendix gives an empirical-equivalent employee-year specification with PERFORMANCE, ABILITY, and PROMTYPE measures.
The appendix defines PROMTYPE at t+1 by promotion status and describes the next-year/current-job versus first-year/next-job performance outcome.

evidence.description: The bounded static inventory lists only moers_online_appendix.pdf, with no entry points or supported code artifacts.

actions.description: Obtain the author-provided executable package and its workflow/data instructions before assessing full-pipeline execution.
steps: Request or locate the source files and README/data guide that implement the empirical analysis; identify each entry point, required stage, supporting program, and producer-consumer handoff.

Request the exact analysis inputs and their required stored fields, identifiers, period/coverage, construction, format, and author-documented acquisition or preparation route for PERFORMANCE, ABILITY, and PROMTYPE.

After the workflow is supplied, inventory all mandatory branches and assess each input and prescribed software against the documented route; do not independently reconstruct the historical study data.
validation: Confirm every documented stage has a supplied source/entry point or a specifically recorded unresolved dependency, and verify producer-consumer order from the actual workflow.
Verify candidate input fields, identifiers, construction, and coverage against the author specification before recording any local or public route as compatible.

review_notes: This is a document-only release of the online appendix. The empirical model provides limited variable context, but it does not document executable code, the full workflow, or compatible analysis inputs.
